justification: Battle-axe detection flagged ~51 of 1,200 real lots, ~8 real (precision ~16-18%): it measured width along map axes, so tilted lots, triangles and wedges looked like handles (e.g. 42-44 Albert St Belmore). New rule straightens the lot and needs an even-width strip that opens suddenly; precision 1.00 and recall 0.92 on 64 labelled real lots; widths in true metres (projected distance / Mercator scale).

functions.name: detectBattleaxeLot
functions.input: a lot ring in Web Mercator from the cadastre lookup
functions.output: isBattleaxe plus strip width and length, main lot width, length and area
functions.if_none: missing or short ring returns not a battle-axe with zero measurements

break_it.scenario: a wide normal lot sits at 45 degrees to the map grid
break_it.what_happens: old code saw pointed ends and flagged a handle
break_it.repro: detectBattleaxeLot on a 40 x 15 m rectangle rotated 45 degrees
break_it.how: lot is straightened to its minimum-area rectangle first; test covers 0-63 degrees

break_it.scenario: a triangular or wedge lot narrows to a point at one end
break_it.what_happens: the narrow end looked like a handle
break_it.repro: labelled fixture triangles from St Ives
break_it.how: strip must be even width within 1.3x and open suddenly to 3x wider

break_it.scenario: a rural battle-axe has a 9 m wide access strip
break_it.what_happens: an 8 m cap would miss it
break_it.repro: Bowral fixture lots with 8.8-9.2 m strips
break_it.how: strip cap is 12 m; recall 0.91 on labels

break_it.scenario: a cut corner at the street end makes the strip look uneven
break_it.what_happens: a real strip is rejected as uneven
break_it.repro: fixture lot with a 5 m corner slice then 9 m strip
break_it.how: end slices under 0.75 of the strip median are trimmed

break_it.scenario: a winding long private road serves the lot
break_it.what_happens: uneven width so the rule misses it (known miss)
break_it.how: accepted: 1 of 11 real lots missed; next step would use the road-frontage layer

break_it.scenario: projected distances are multiplied by the Mercator scale factor instead of divided
break_it.what_happens: every width is ~1.46x too large and real 3 m strips read as 4.4 m
break_it.repro: detectBattleaxeLot on a 3 m strip scaled by 1.205
break_it.how: k = 1 / scaleFactorForRing; jest asserts the 3 m strip measures 2.9-3.1 m

break_it.scenario: a flag lot widens in two steps from a wide 18 m stem (38 Park Rd Bowral)
break_it.what_happens: a single 3x jump test misses it
break_it.repro: detectBattleaxeLot on the Bowral ring in the fixture
break_it.how: first step needs 2x, main lot must reach 3x; min strip length 8 m stops tapered corners

post_merge.manual_verify: GET /api/property for 42-44 Albert St Belmore (no battle-axe) and 38 Park Rd Bowral (battle-axe)

falsifiable_check.fails_when: precision or recall on the labelled real lots drops below 0.9, or a tilted rectangle is flagged
falsifiable_check.observed_red: old detector on the same fixture: precision 0.18 (fails the 0.9 floor)
